purpose: A bounded, evidence-first method for deciding which residential water-treatment offer, if any, a specific household should be shown: segmenting the territory and the prospect by water source and water-problem class, building the diagnosis from real evidence (the utility's published water-quality report, a dated in-home screening panel, the premise plumbing itself, and accredited-laboratory escalation where a health-based standard or a microbiological question is in play), interpreting results against published standard classes without medical or fear-based claims, mapping only confirmed problems onto the treatment mechanism classes that verifiably address them, scoping point-of-use against point-of-entry, and packaging certified, fully disclosed offer tiers whose price is a traceable build-up of real distributor, labour, permit and warranty-reserve inputs rather than an invented figure.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator sells and installs residential water treatment (softening, scale conditioning, filtration, reverse osmosis and disinfection classes) and earns on equipment, installation and recurring filter and service work
the person being sold to owns the dwelling being treated, or an owner's written authorisation is obtained at intake before any point-of-entry work is proposed

water chemistry is site-specific and time-varying: a utility's annual report, a neighbour's result and a test strip are all weaker evidence than a dated sample taken from this tap by a stated protocol

plumbing code, permitting, contractor licensing, brine and reject-water discharge rules, home-solicitation cancellation rights and advertising-substantiation duties are real obligation classes whose current specifics must be verified with the authority having jurisdiction; this knowledge base names the class and never asserts the rule text

equipment cost, labour cost, permit fees and finance participation are knowable per deal from documents the operator already holds, so every money statement here is a mechanism to be filled in from those documents
exclusions: sizing equipment to household demand and water chemistry, equipment placement, bypass and drain design, permit filing, the physical installation, leak-risk control and commissioning - that territory belongs to the system sizing, installation and plumbing-compliance knowledge base

filter-replacement schedules per treatment class, service-plan tier design, reminder and scheduling systems, retest cadence as proof of value, churn analysis and referral loops - that territory belongs to the filter service plans and retention knowledge base

any health, medical or physiological claim about water or treatment; findings are stated as chemistry compared with published standard classes, never as a diagnosis, a prognosis or a promise of a health outcome
fear-based or urgency-manufactured selling, including any demonstration staged to imply contamination the chemistry does not show, and any expiring same-visit discount

invented prices, margins, commissions, close rates or market sizes; money appears only as mechanism (which cost inputs exist, how a quote is built up, what moves margin) and is verified per deal against the actual distributor quote, timesheet, permit receipt and finance schedule
personalised financial, legal, tax, medical or insurance advice; this is operator education about running a water-treatment business
commercial, industrial, municipal and agricultural water treatment; the scope is residential point-of-use and point-of-entry systems
well drilling, pump replacement, pressure-tank and septic work, which are referred to licensed well and plumbing contractors rather than solved with a filter

competency_questions.question: Before we spend a truck roll, which parts of this territory are worth working, and what water problem class should we expect at a given address?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TERRITORY_WATER_PROFILE resolves each neighbourhood to a named community water system or to private-well status with its published evidence, and PROBLEM_CLASS_SEGMENTATION names the problem classes that expectation maps to

competency_questions.question: What must the first phone or web contact establish before we book a test visit, and when is the honest answer that we should not visit at all?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAD_INTAKE_QUALIFICATION lists the facts captured (supply type, symptoms and their history, ownership and authority, prior testing, existing equipment, who will be present) and the disqualification and referral rules

competency_questions.question: What are we allowed to say about what our equipment does, what must we never say about water and health, and how do we answer a competitor's scare pitch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_CLAIM_BOUNDARY gives the permitted mechanism-claim form and the banned-claim list, CERTIFICATION_VETTING supplies the per-model evidence behind a claim, and COMPETITIVE_MISINFO_HANDLING gives the mechanism-not-mudslinging rebuttal routine

competency_questions.question: How do we conduct a visit with an elderly, distressed or limited-English homeowner so that a sale, if it happens, is one they would still endorse a week later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VULNERABLE_CONSUMER_CARE states the vulnerability signals and the procedural safeguards, and IN_HOME_VISIT_PROTOCOL states the disclosure-first choreography and the prohibition on manufactured urgency

competency_questions.question: What does the utility's annual water-quality report tell us about this address, and what can it never tell us?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MUNICIPAL_REPORT_READING names what the report supports (source, disinfectant, reported hardness, detected regulated parameters, violations) and what it cannot support (this tap today, premise plumbing contributions, private wells)

competency_questions.question: Which tests do we run in the home, what does each instrument actually measure, and how do we show a result without overstating it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIELD_SCREENING_PANEL states per-instrument meaning and limits and the dated screening record, and HONEST_DEMO_PROTOCOL states which demonstrations are permitted, which are banned, and the control requirement

competency_questions.question: At what point must screening stop and an accredited laboratory take over, how is the sample taken, and who pays for it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCREDITED_LAB_ESCALATION lists the mandatory escalation triggers, the sampling and chain-of-custody protocol, and a stated who-pays policy that does not condition the result on a purchase

competency_questions.question: How do we compare a laboratory result to published standards and explain an exceedance without making a health claim?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STANDARDS_INTERPRETATION separates health-based from aesthetic standard classes, handles reporting limits and non-detects honestly, and states the stopping rule that ends interpretation at chemistry and treatment class

competency_questions.question: What in the house itself - fixtures, water heater, plumbing material and era, existing equipment - counts as evidence, and what does it change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREMISE_EVIDENCE_SURVEY lists the observations captured with photographs and dates and states which of them change the sampling protocol or the recommendation

competency_questions.question: A private-well household calls: how is the diagnostic path different, and when is the right answer a well contractor rather than a treatment system?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WELL_OWNER_PATH covers well construction and surroundings, the bacteriological and nitrate testing recommendation class with a verify-locally flag, and the referral rule when the defect is the well

competency_questions.question: Given the confirmed problems, which treatment classes verifiably address them, and which common pairings are simply wrong?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TREATMENT_CLASS_MECHANISMS explains each class by physical mechanism and its preconditions, and PROBLEM_TO_CLASS_MAPPING gives the evidence-to-class mapping plus the named anti-pattern list

competency_questions.question: Should this household be treated at the whole house, at a single tap, or both, and how are the options packaged so they can be compared?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POU_VS_POE_SCOPING gives the treat-where decision rule with household constraints recorded, and OFFER_TIER_ARCHITECTURE shows tiers differentiated by real mechanism, capacity, certification or warranty rather than by discount ladder

competency_questions.question: How is the price of this specific job built up, what moves the margin, and how is every input verified for this deal?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICE_MARGIN_MECHANICS enumerates the cost stack and the levers that move it and requires per-deal verification against real documents, and QUOTE_DISCLOSURE_PACKET shows how those lines are itemised to the customer

competency_questions.question: What exactly must be written down and handed over before an installation date is promised or a service plan is enrolled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIAGNOSTIC_DOSSIER_HANDOFF lists the dossier contents (dated chemistry, accepted and excluded problem classes, chosen classes with certification listings, premise facts, constraints, signed disclosures, implied consumables, open questions) and states the no-install-date gate

glossary.definition: Treatment installed on the main service line so every fixture in the dwelling receives treated water; the correct scope when the problem damages plumbing or affects all outlets, and the scope that raises drain, space, bypass and permitting questions handled by the installation knowledge base.

Treatment installed at a single outlet, typically an under-sink drinking-water system or a refrigerator line; the honest scope when the concern is drinking and cooking water only, and often the smaller and correct recommendation.

A resin bed that exchanges calcium and magnesium ions for sodium or potassium and is periodically regenerated with brine; it removes hardness and returns an equivalent quantity of the exchanged ion to the water, and its brine discharge is subject to local sewer and septic rules that must be verified with the authority having jurisdiction.

A salt-free class that converts dissolved hardness into microcrystals which resist adhering to hot surfaces; it inhibits scale without removing hardness, so a hardness test downstream still reads hard and the slippery softened-water feel never appears - a difference that must be stated before purchase.

A carbon sub-class whose surface is treated to accelerate reactions that plain activated carbon handles poorly, used where the district disinfects with chloramine or where hydrogen sulfide is present; specifying it requires knowing which disinfectant the utility actually uses.

A pressure-driven membrane process that rejects a broad range of dissolved species and sends a reject stream to drain; normally deployed as a point-of-use drinking-water system with sediment and carbon stages before and after the membrane.

The annual water-quality report class that community water systems publish for their customers, covering source water, treatment, detected regulated parameters and any violations for a reporting period; what it must contain and where it is posted varies by jurisdiction and must be verified locally.

A laboratory holding current certification or accreditation from the state or national programme that governs drinking-water analysis, using its own bottles, preservatives and holding times; its dated report is the evidence class that a field strip or meter reading can only point toward.

The distinction between enforceable health-based drinking-water limits and non-enforceable aesthetic or secondary values covering taste, odour, colour and staining; the class determines whether a result is a compliance matter for the supplier or a comfort matter for the household, and current values must be confirmed with the primary regulator.

The lowest concentration a given analytical method can reliably quantify, below which a laboratory reports a non-detect; a non-detect therefore means 'below this method's reporting limit', never 'none present', and honest interpretation states the limit alongside the result.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for water_treatment_offer_and_honest_diagnostics work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Build and maintain a working map of the service area by water supply rather than by postal code: which neighbourhoods are served by which community water systems, which are on private wells, what each utility publishes about its source (surface, groundwater, blended, seasonally switched), which disinfectant it carries (free chlorine or chloramine), what hardness it reports, and which pockets carry a known regional signature such as iron and manganese staining, hydrogen-sulfide odour, nitrate in irrigated agricultural groundwater, or aggressive low-pH water. The profile is assembled from published utility water-quality reports, state and county groundwater and well records, and the operator's own accumulating file of dated customer results, and it decides where marketing money goes, which media, cartridges and test reagents ride on the van, and what the technician expects before the door opens - while never standing in for a test of the actual tap being sold to.

included: utility-by-utility source, disinfectant and hardness profile
well versus municipal neighbourhood map
regional problem signatures with the dated published source each came from
the operator's own accumulated result history treated as territory data
excluded: the individual household's confirmed chemistry, which only a dated sample from that tap establishes
equipment sizing, placement and install logistics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a utility publishes a new annual report or changes source or disinfectant, or the operator's own accumulated test results contradict the profiled signature of a district

pros.claim: Knowing the disinfectant and hardness signature of each district before the visit puts the right reagents, media and literature on the van and shortens the appointment
pros.example: arriving in a chloraminated district with a total-chlorine reagent and catalytic-carbon literature instead of a free-chlorine strip and a plain carbon brochure

pros.claim: A supply map lets marketing spend follow the problem rather than the postal code, because well pockets and hard-water districts need different messages
pros.example: running well-testing content in the unincorporated fringe while running scale-and-appliance content in the hardest municipal district

cons.claim: A territory profile silently becomes a stereotype, and an averaged utility figure invites quoting a number for a house nobody has tested
cons.example: telling a homeowner their water is a certain hardness because the district report says so, when their street sits on a blended zone that runs materially different

cons.claim: The profile decays quietly, since utilities change source and disinfectant without telling equipment dealers
cons.example: specifying plain carbon for months after a district switched to chloramine and then fielding taste complaints

failure_modes: treating a system-wide annual average as this household's water
mapping by postal code when service-area boundaries cut across it
letting the profile go stale after a source change, a new blended well or a disinfectant switch
acceptance_tests: every neighbourhood the company serves resolves either to a named community water system or to private-well status, each with the dated published document it came from
each profiled district records its disinfectant type and the date of the report that established it
revisit_triggers: a utility publishes a new annual report, changes source, blends a new well or switches disinfectant
accumulated in-territory customer results diverge from what the published profile implied

nodes.definition: Fix in writing, before anyone knocks on a door, the exact perimeter of what this company may assert. Inside the line sit mechanism statements tied to a treatment class and, where a product is involved, to a third-party certification held by that specific model for that specific claim: a softener exchanges hardness minerals so scale stops forming on the heater and fixtures, activated carbon reduces chlorine taste and odour, a certified reverse-osmosis system reduces the listed dissolved contaminants at that tap. Outside the line sit every health, medical or physiological claim, every implication that the household's water is making someone ill, every 'toxic' or 'poison' framing, every disease-prevention suggestion, and every claim that outruns either the certification listing or the test data actually in hand. The perimeter governs advertising copy, social posts and door-hanger text exactly as it governs the living-room conversation, because the substantiation duty class applies to the claim wherever it is made; verify the current advertising and consumer-protection rules for your jurisdiction, and keep the certification listing or dated laboratory report filed with the claim it supports.

included: the permitted mechanism-claim form
the banned-claim list including all health and disease framing
advertising, web and social copy under the same rule
the substantiation file that pairs each claim with its listing or lab report
excluded: the technical lookup of a certification listing
rebutting a specific competitor's pitch
the sizing and installation claims owned by the installation knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an advertising or consumer-protection rule change, a certification listing change, or a complaint alleging a health claim was made in the home

pros.claim: A written claim perimeter converts an ethics preference into something a new salesperson can be trained on and audited against
pros.example: a ride-along scorecard that marks a representative as failed for saying 'this is why your family keeps getting sick', whether or not the job closed

pros.claim: Claims that never exceed the evidence survive complaints, reviews and regulator questions without retraction
pros.example: answering a consumer-protection enquiry by producing the certification listing and the dated laboratory report behind every line of the quote

cons.claim: The honest claim is less viscerally persuasive than the fear claim, so close rates can sit below those of rivals who sell on alarm
cons.example: losing a decision to a competitor who calls the same municipal water 'toxic' after running a precipitator demonstration

cons.claim: Policing tone as well as words is slow, because a raised eyebrow can carry the health implication that the script forbids
cons.example: a representative who says only 'here is the nitrate result' but pauses meaningfully at the word 'infants' until the customer supplies the fear themselves

failure_modes: letting a health implication ride in tone, pause or gesture while the words stay compliant
claiming a certification the specific model does not hold, or a claim broader than the listing
website and social copy drifting past what the in-home script allows because nobody audits it
acceptance_tests: every claim used in the field or in advertising maps to a named treatment mechanism plus either a current certification listing for that exact model and claim or a dated test result from this address
no artifact in the sales kit, on the website or in social copy contains a health, disease or 'toxic water' assertion
a sampled ride-along review finds no health implication delivered by wording, tone or implication
revisit_triggers: a regulator, platform or trade association updates advertising substantiation expectations
a manufacturer changes, narrows or loses a certification listing the sales kit relies on
a customer complaint alleges that something said in the home crossed into a health claim

nodes.definition: Sort demand into the small set of problem classes that genuinely drive different diagnostics, different equipment and different conversations, instead of treating 'bad water' as one market. The working classes are hardness and scale (spotting, crusted aerators, soap and appliance complaints, heater life), taste and odour (chlorine bite, chloramine flatness, sulfur smell, musty or earthy notes), staining and sediment (orange or brown iron, black manganese, cloudy or gritty water), specific-contaminant concern (nitrate in agricultural groundwater, lead originating in premise plumbing, arsenic in certain aquifers, a per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance worry following a news cycle), and microbiological risk, which in residential work is essentially a private-well class. Each class carries a different burden of proof, a different mechanism family, a different urgency and a different failure mode when misdiagnosed; households commonly sit in two or three at once, and the segmentation exists precisely to keep those strands separate through diagnosis, offer and handover instead of collapsing them into one appliance.

included: the five working problem classes and their distinguishing symptoms
the burden of proof each class demands
the rule that a household may sit in several classes at once
excluded: the treatment class selected for a confirmed problem
capacity sizing and regeneration settings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a pattern of complaints or post-install dissatisfaction that the current class set does not describe

pros.claim: Separating classes defeats the everything-is-a-softener reflex and preserves the case for a second, different device
pros.example: a hard-water household whose real complaint is chlorine taste ends up with softening plus a drinking-water stage rather than a softener that never touched the taste

pros.claim: Class-specific burdens of proof stop an aesthetic complaint from being answered with contaminant language
pros.example: handling a musty odour as a taste-and-odour class question rather than as a contamination scare

cons.claim: Multi-class households can be walked into an over-broad recommendation because every strand is technically real
cons.example: adding an iron filter for a faint intermittent stain that a laundry-habit change and a heater flush would have resolved

cons.claim: Customer language does not map cleanly onto the classes, so early classification can misdirect the whole visit
cons.example: 'my water is dirty' meaning air entrainment, cloudy hot water, sediment after a main break, or simply a stained toilet, each with a different path

failure_modes: classifying from the customer's phrase rather than from a symptom the technician can observe
collapsing several live classes into the single class the company most likes selling
treating a specific-contaminant concern as an aesthetic one because a strip showed nothing
acceptance_tests: every open opportunity carries one or more named problem classes, and each named class points at the evidence that would confirm or eliminate it
a household with several classes has each strand tracked separately through to the recommendation
revisit_triggers: a recurring complaint pattern appears that none of the existing classes describes well
post-install dissatisfaction shows a class was recorded but never addressed

nodes.definition: Run the first phone or web contact as a structured intake that settles, before a truck moves, the facts that change everything downstream: whether the address is on a community water system or a private well; what the household actually notices, in their own words, and since when; whether the caller owns the property or needs an owner's authorisation; whether anyone has tested the water and whether a report or utility notice exists; whether treatment equipment is already installed, by whom, and when it was last serviced; who the decision-makers are and whether all of them can be present; and whether there is an obvious site constraint worth flagging early, such as no nearby drain, an unknown main shut-off, a well pit or a homeowner-association restriction. Intake also disqualifies honestly and cheaply: tenants without owner authority are routed to the owner, callers whose symptom points at a pump, a heater or a plumbing failure are referred to the right trade, and callers who open with a health goal are told plainly, at that moment, that treatment is sold on chemistry and never on a health promise.

included: the intake question set and its record
ownership and authorisation check
existing-equipment and prior-testing capture
disqualification and cross-trade referral rules
the early health-claim reset
excluded: the in-home survey and testing themselves
scheduling logistics and route density

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rise in wasted or aborted visits traced to a fact the intake script does not capture

pros.claim: Establishing supply type and ownership on the call prevents the two most expensive wasted visits in the trade
pros.example: discovering on the phone that the caller rents, so the appointment is rebooked with the owner instead of ending at the door

pros.claim: Capturing symptom history in the customer's own words gives the technician a hypothesis to test rather than a blank page
pros.example: 'the smell only comes from the hot tap and only in the morning' pointing the visit at the water heater rather than at the supply

cons.claim: A long intake script suppresses booking rates, especially for callers who simply want someone to come and look
cons.example: a caller abandoning the call at the ownership and decision-maker questions and phoning a competitor who books in ninety seconds

cons.claim: Phone-reported symptoms are unreliable and can anchor the technician on the wrong class before arrival
cons.example: a reported 'rotten egg smell' that turns out to be a sacrificial anode reaction in the heater rather than sulfide in the supply

failure_modes: booking a point-of-entry appointment without confirming who may authorise work on the plumbing
failing to ask about existing equipment and arriving to find a competitor's softener under warranty
letting a caller's health framing stand unchallenged so the visit starts on a promise the company cannot make
acceptance_tests: every booked visit has an intake record with supply type, symptoms and their history, ownership and authority, prior testing, existing equipment, and who will attend
every disqualified or referred caller has the reason recorded and the trade they were referred to
revisit_triggers: booked-to-completed visit ratios fall or wasted trips rise for a recognisable reason
technicians repeatedly report a fact at the door that intake should have caught

nodes.definition: Treat some households as requiring extra procedural care rather than extra persuasion: elderly homeowners living alone, people showing confusion or cognitive difficulty, households conducting the conversation in a language the representative does not speak well, recently bereaved or otherwise distressed occupants, and anyone whose questions reveal that they do not follow what is being proposed. The safeguards are procedural, teachable and auditable - offer to include a family member or trusted second person and pause the visit until they can attend, keep the quoted price valid long enough that the decision can be slept on, never let a discount expire with the appointment, use a competent interpreter rather than a nodding relative for anything contractual, hand over and read aloud the written cancellation-rights notice that the home-solicitation obligation class in your jurisdiction requires and verify that current requirement locally, and stop the visit outright when the person cannot explain back in their own words what they are buying, what it will fix and what it will cost.

included: the vulnerability signal list
the second-person, cooling-off and interpreter safeguards
the explain-it-back stop rule
the cancellation-notice obligation class flagged for local verification
excluded: the general visit choreography applied to every household
financing product selection and underwriting

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint or cancellation alleging pressure, or a change in the local home-solicitation cancellation-rights requirement class

pros.claim: Procedural safeguards protect the household and the company at the same time, because a sale that survives a family review survives everything else
pros.example: an adult daughter reviewing the quote two days later and confirming the order instead of demanding a cancellation and posting a review

pros.claim: An explain-it-back rule catches misunderstanding that politeness hides
pros.example: a homeowner who nods throughout but then describes the proposed softener as something that will make the water safe to drink, which stops the sale until the difference is understood

cons.claim: Deferring decisions costs same-visit closes and some deferred customers never buy at all
cons.example: pausing an obviously affordable and well-evidenced job for a week so a relative can attend, and losing it to a competitor who signs that evening

cons.claim: Vulnerability is judged in minutes on incomplete information, so the rule is applied unevenly between representatives
cons.example: one technician treating a sharp eighty-year-old engineer as vulnerable while another misses genuine confusion in a much younger customer

failure_modes: using a family member as an interpreter for contract terms they themselves do not understand
letting an expiring discount create exactly the pressure the safeguards exist to remove
recording the safeguards in policy while the field never applies them because nothing is audited
acceptance_tests: any visit flagged for a vulnerability signal shows the safeguard applied, the cancellation notice handed over, and the price held beyond the visit
the file records the customer's own explain-back of what the system does and does not do before any signature
revisit_triggers: a cancellation, chargeback or family complaint alleges pressure on a vulnerable household
the home-solicitation cancellation obligation class in a served jurisdiction changes

nodes.definition: For every address on a community water system, retrieve and read the supplier's annual water-quality report - the consumer confidence report class published under the drinking-water regulation of your jurisdiction, whose required contents and posting location must be verified locally - and mine it for exactly what it can support: which source waters feed the district, whether the plant carries free chlorine or chloramine, the reported hardness, the regulated parameters detected with their ranges and the standard each is compared against, and any violation, monitoring lapse or public notice from the reporting period. Just as important is teaching, out loud, what the report cannot support: it describes water leaving the plant and sampled points in the distribution system across a reporting period, usually as averages and ranges; it says nothing about what this household's service line, premise plumbing, water heater or existing softener contributes after the meter, nothing at all about a private well, and nothing about what came out of this kitchen tap this morning.

included: retrieving the current report for the serving system
extracting source, disinfectant, hardness, detected parameters and violations
stating the report's coverage limits to the customer
excluded: private-well households, which have no such report
any conclusion about this tap that only a dated sample can support

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: publication of a new annual report, a public notice, or a source or disinfectant change in the serving district

pros.claim: The report is free, public and dated, which makes it the cheapest credible evidence a visit can open with
pros.example: opening the conversation with the district's own published disinfectant and hardness figures rather than with a sales claim

pros.claim: Reading it before the visit prevents specifying the wrong carbon class and prevents 'discovering' a contaminant the utility already reports and treats
pros.example: seeing chloramine disinfection in the report and specifying catalytic carbon before the appointment is even booked

cons.claim: The report is an aggregate over a period and a system, so it can be simultaneously accurate and irrelevant to one house
cons.example: a district-wide average that hides a blended zone, a dead-end main, or the household's own aged galvanised service line

cons.claim: Its language is compliance language, and homeowners misread detected-but-compliant results as alarming
cons.example: a customer reading a compliant disinfection by-product entry as proof of a danger the report was in fact demonstrating was within the standard

failure_modes: quoting a report figure as this household's water
using an out-of-date report after a source or disinfectant change
weaponising a detected-but-compliant entry to manufacture concern
acceptance_tests: the current report for the serving system is attached to the opportunity file with its reporting period and retrieval date
the customer-facing summary states in one sentence what the report does not cover, including premise plumbing and this tap today
revisit_triggers: a new annual report is published or a public notice is issued for the district
the utility changes source, blends a new supply or switches disinfectant

nodes.definition: Run a materially different diagnostic for private-well households, because no utility tests their water and the owner is in practice the operator of their own supply. The path begins with the well rather than the water: age, depth and construction where records exist, casing and cap condition, wellhead grading and any history of flooding or standing water, separation from the septic field, livestock or cultivated ground, and any recent change such as a new pump, a drawn-down season, a nearby drilling job or work done on the well itself. Only then does it reach chemistry. Testing here is not decoration: bacteriological and nitrate analysis through an accredited laboratory is the recommendation class published by public-health agencies for well owners, and the current guidance, sampling instructions and any free or subsidised county programme must be verified where you operate. That result decides which of three honest answers applies - a treatment system, a well disinfection and re-test before anything is sold, or a referral to a licensed well contractor because the defect is the well and no filter will fix it.

included: well construction, surroundings and history questionnaire
the bacteriological and nitrate testing recommendation class with a verify-locally flag
seasonal and post-event retest logic
the referral rule when the defect is the well
excluded: well drilling, pump and pressure-tank repair, and septic work
disinfection equipment sizing and installation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in public-health well-testing guidance, a county testing programme, or observed seasonal variation in results from wells in the territory

pros.claim: Inspecting the well before the water finds causes that no treatment system would have addressed
pros.example: a cracked well cap and ponding at the head explaining recurring coliform far better than any filter specification would

pros.claim: Well households are naturally recurring customers because their supply has no operator but them, which supports honest annual retesting
pros.example: a household that retests annually after spring recharge because the first result showed seasonal variation

cons.claim: Well work exposes the company to the temptation of selling equipment as a substitute for a well repair the owner would rather not pay for
cons.example: a customer asking for ultraviolet disinfection instead of fixing an obviously compromised casing

cons.claim: Well chemistry moves with season, water table and use, so a single sample can misrepresent the supply in either direction
cons.example: a clean late-summer sample from a well that goes coliform-positive every spring

failure_modes: selling treatment on top of a structurally compromised well
treating one sample as the well's permanent character
skipping the bacteriological test because the water looks and tastes fine
acceptance_tests: every well opportunity has a completed well-history and wellhead observation record with photographs
no disinfection or contaminant-specific system is proposed for a well without an accredited-laboratory result for the relevant parameter
any structural well defect observed is written into the file with the referral made
revisit_triggers: a seasonal change, flood, nearby drilling or pump replacement occurs at the property
public-health guidance or a county subsidised testing programme for well owners changes

nodes.definition: Define the panel a technician actually runs at the kitchen sink and, instrument by instrument, what it measures and what it cannot. Hardness by titration drops or strip yields a working figure that sizes the softening conversation; a total-dissolved-solids meter reads electrical conductivity converted to an estimated mineral content and is in no sense a contamination meter; free-chlorine and total-chlorine reagents distinguish a free-chlorine district from a chloraminated one and therefore decide the carbon specification; pH, iron, manganese, hydrogen-sulfide odour and nitrate strips are coarse indicators with real detection limits, interferences and colour-reading subjectivity. Every reading is written on a dated form that records the sample point, whether the line was flushed and for how long, hot or cold, and the method used; every reading is described to the homeowner as a screening indication rather than an analysis; and any reading that touches a health-based parameter is treated strictly as a trigger for laboratory confirmation, never as a finding to sell against.

included: the instrument-by-instrument panel and its meaning
sampling point, flush state and method recording
the screening-not-analysis language rule
the escalate-on-health-parameter trigger
excluded: accredited laboratory analysis and its chain of custody
demonstrations performed for persuasion rather than measurement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: repeated disagreement between field readings and accredited-laboratory results, or a change of reagent, meter or method

pros.claim: A standard panel makes visits comparable across technicians and turns loose impressions into a dated record
pros.example: two technicians in the same district producing hardness and chlorine results that can be compared because both recorded flush time and sample point

pros.claim: Screening cheaply eliminates whole hypotheses before anyone pays for laboratory work
pros.example: a strong hardness reading and an absent iron reading redirecting a suspected staining complaint to scale and soap residue

cons.claim: Field instruments carry real error and interference, and a confident-looking number invites over-reading
cons.example: a colour-comparison strip read under warm kitchen lighting producing an iron result the laboratory does not reproduce

cons.claim: A total-dissolved-solids reading is the single most misused number in the trade because customers hear purity where the meter reports minerals
cons.example: a customer concluding that a higher reading than their neighbour's means their water is unsafe

failure_modes: presenting a screening reading as an analysis
sampling from an aerator, a softened line or a hot tap without recording it
using a dissolved-solids reading as an implied contamination score
acceptance_tests: every screening result on file records sample point, flush state, temperature, method and date, and is labelled as screening
no health-based parameter appears in a recommendation on the strength of a field reading alone
the customer-facing explanation of the dissolved-solids reading states that it measures dissolved mineral content and not safety
revisit_triggers: laboratory results repeatedly contradict field readings for a given parameter
a reagent or meter is replaced, recalibrated or found past its expiry

nodes.definition: Read the house itself as evidence, because the plumbing records a longer history than any single sample. The survey walks fixtures, kettle, showerheads, aerators and toilet tanks for scale and staining and notes which colour the staining is and where it concentrates; ages the water heater and looks for sediment noise, a discharging relief valve or a previously replaced element; identifies plumbing material and era - copper with lead-bearing solder, galvanised steel, polybutylene, cross-linked polyethylene - because material and era set the premise-plumbing lead-risk class and therefore whether a first-draw sampling protocol is required; locates the main shut-off and notes static pressure; and inventories any existing softener, cartridge housing or reverse-osmosis unit along with its bypass position, media or cartridge age and whether it has ever been serviced. Everything is photographed and dated. The survey gathers facts and constraints only: where equipment could physically go, how it would be sized, drained, supported and permitted is the installation knowledge base's decision and is deliberately not made here.

included: fixture, heater and staining observation
plumbing material and era identification as a lead-risk class signal
existing-equipment inventory and condition
dated photographs and recorded constraints
excluded: placement, sizing, drain and bypass design decisions
any repair of the plumbing itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: installer feedback that a site fact was missed, or plumbing and equipment changes at the property

pros.claim: Physical evidence corroborates or contradicts the water sample and often explains an intermittent complaint
pros.example: heavy scale on the showerhead and a fifteen-year-old heater confirming a long-standing hardness problem the household had stopped noticing

pros.claim: Identifying plumbing era changes the sampling protocol before the sample is taken, which prevents a wasted laboratory run
pros.example: an era of lead-bearing solder prompting a first-draw sample from the kitchen cold tap instead of a flushed one

cons.claim: Observation without measurement invites narrative, and a stained fixture can be blamed on the water when the cause is the fixture
cons.example: attributing a rust ring to supply iron when the culprit is a corroding steel toilet-tank component

cons.claim: The survey uncovers plumbing defects the company is neither licensed nor asked to fix, which complicates the visit
cons.example: finding an actively weeping shut-off valve that must be disclosed and referred before any installation is scheduled

failure_modes: skipping the existing-equipment inventory and mis-attributing treated water to the supply
failing to note that the sampled tap sits downstream of an existing softener or filter
recording observations without dated photographs so nothing survives the argument later
acceptance_tests: the file records plumbing material and era, heater age, main shut-off location, static pressure and any existing equipment with its condition
every claimed physical symptom has a dated photograph attached
the sampling point's position relative to any existing treatment is recorded
revisit_triggers: plumbing work, a heater replacement or new equipment is installed at the property
the installer reports a site fact the survey missed

nodes.definition: Govern what may be demonstrated in a living room. A demonstration is permitted when it teaches real chemistry, is explained before it is run, is reproducible by the homeowner afterwards, and is narrated in terms of what it does and does not prove: the soap-lather or titration comparison that shows hardness and the same test on softened water; a chlorine reagent whose colour change is named aloud as a chlorine indicator and nothing more; a before-and-after dissolved-solids reading across a reverse-osmosis membrane described as mineral content falling, not as poison being removed. Banned outright are the traps of the trade - the electrolysis precipitator that flocculates dissolved minerals out of almost any ordinary water while the representative says 'look what is in your water', reagents chosen because they colour the sample dramatically while contamination is implied by silence, and any test run on the customer's water without the same test being run on a known control such as bottled water or the company's own treated sample. The governing rule is simple: if the homeowner would feel tricked once they understood the chemistry, it is not a demonstration, it is theatre, and it is prohibited whatever it closes.

included: the permitted demonstration list and its narration rules
the mandatory control sample
the banned-demonstration list
the would-feel-tricked test
excluded: quantitative screening and laboratory analysis
rebuttal of a competitor's demonstration after the fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a customer or regulator report that a demonstration was understood as contamination proof, or a new competitor demonstration circulating in the territory

pros.claim: A demonstration the customer can repeat converts a claim into something they own, which survives the sceptical relative who arrives later
pros.example: a homeowner repeating the soap-shake hardness comparison for a spouse that evening and getting the same result

pros.claim: Banning precipitator theatre removes the company's largest single reputational exposure in this trade
pros.example: being able to answer a consumer-protection complaint by showing that no electrolysis device has ever been on the vans

cons.claim: Honest demonstrations are visually dull next to the banned ones, so representatives feel disarmed against rivals who use them
cons.example: a titration colour change competing poorly against a rival's tank of orange flocculant on the same street

cons.claim: Even permitted demonstrations mislead if narration slips, because customers remember the visual and forget the caveat
cons.example: a dissolved-solids drop across a membrane remembered as 'it took the contaminants out' despite a correct explanation at the time

failure_modes: running any demonstration on the customer's water without a control
letting silence after a dramatic visual do the implying that the script forbids
carrying a banned device on the van for 'training purposes' where it will inevitably be used
acceptance_tests: no banned demonstration device is present in any vehicle or sales kit, verified on a recurring kit audit
every demonstration performed in a home is recorded with the control that accompanied it
the written leave-behind repeats what each demonstration did and did not show
revisit_triggers: a competitor demonstration circulating locally requires a documented, mechanism-based response
a customer reports having understood a demonstration as proof of contamination

nodes.definition: Know the line at which screening stops and a certified laboratory takes over, and cross it without hesitation or negotiation. Escalation is mandatory for anything with a health-based standard or a microbiological question: coliform and E. coli on any private well, nitrate wherever agricultural groundwater or an infant in the household makes the regulated limit the relevant comparison, lead wherever premise-plumbing era or a first-draw concern exists, arsenic in aquifers known for it, and any contaminant the homeowner names from a news cycle including per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances. Escalation also means sampling correctly: the laboratory's own bottles and preservatives, its specified first-draw or flushed protocol, the sample point, time and temperature recorded, chain of custody honoured, holding times respected, and turnaround stated honestly to the customer. Who pays is decided by written policy in advance - absorbed as the cost of a serious diagnosis, credited against a purchase, or routed to a county or health-department programme where one exists - and the result belongs to the homeowner in every case, delivered whether or not anything is ever bought.

included: the mandatory escalation trigger list
sampling protocol, preservation and chain of custody
the who-pays policy and result ownership
honest turnaround communication
excluded: interpreting the returned result against standards
performing analysis in-house

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in laboratory accreditation, methods or turnaround, or the appearance of a public testing programme that changes who pays

pros.claim: A laboratory report is the only evidence class strong enough to carry a health-standard parameter into a recommendation
pros.example: a certified lead result from a properly taken first-draw sample supporting a certified drinking-water system at that tap

pros.claim: Delivering the result regardless of purchase builds the referral engine that fear-selling never earns
pros.example: a household that bought nothing after a clean result recommending the company to a neighbour whose well later tested positive

cons.claim: Escalation costs money and days, and it removes the same-visit close from exactly the jobs that feel most urgent
cons.example: waiting on a bacteriological result while the customer, alarmed, buys a system from a competitor who quoted on the spot

cons.claim: Company-paid testing can be read as a conflicted interest unless the laboratory is independent and the report is handed over intact
cons.example: a customer questioning a result until shown that the accredited laboratory, not the company, produced and signed it

failure_modes: sampling into a company bottle or the wrong preservative and invalidating the analysis
flushing a line before a lead first-draw sample and reporting a falsely low result
quoting a system against a health parameter while the laboratory result is still outstanding
acceptance_tests: every health-based or microbiological parameter used in a recommendation traces to a dated accredited-laboratory report with its chain of custody
the sampling protocol used is recorded and matches what the laboratory specified for that parameter
the customer receives the full laboratory report irrespective of whether a purchase follows
revisit_triggers: a laboratory changes accreditation status, method, holding times or turnaround
a subsidised or free public testing programme becomes available in the territory

nodes.definition: Translate a laboratory report into language that is simultaneously accurate and non-medical. The discipline separates the enforceable health-based standard class of the drinking-water regulation applicable where you operate from the aesthetic or secondary class that governs taste, odour, colour and staining, and from advisory or guidance values that are not standards at all; it reads the laboratory's detection and reporting limits so that a non-detect is stated as 'below the reporting limit of this method' rather than as 'none'; it notes that a standard applies to a supplier's delivered water while this sample describes one tap on one date, which is why the comparison is a reference point rather than a verdict on compliance; and it flags that current numeric values must be confirmed with the primary regulator rather than quoted from memory or from a brochure. The stopping rule is absolute: interpretation ends at 'this parameter is above or below the applicable standard, and here is the treatment class that addresses it', and never continues into what it will do to anybody's body.

included: health-based versus aesthetic versus advisory value classes
reporting limits and honest non-detect language
the sample-versus-supply comparison caveat
the stopping rule that forbids health interpretation
excluded: any statement about health effects, which is referred to a physician or the public-health authority
selecting and sizing the treatment equipment itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a regulator revising a standard or advisory value, or a laboratory changing its reporting limits or methods

pros.claim: A disciplined comparison lets a customer act on a real exceedance without being frightened into a purchase
pros.example: explaining that a nitrate result sits above the applicable limit and that two treatment classes address it, then referring health questions to the health department

pros.claim: Stating reporting limits protects the company from the impossible promise of absence
pros.example: writing 'below the reporting limit of this method' rather than 'no lead present' in the quote packet

cons.claim: Careful standard language is harder to follow than the alarm it replaces, and some customers hear hedging
cons.example: a homeowner asking 'so is it safe or not' and being told, correctly, that the parameter is below the standard and that safety questions belong with the health authority

cons.claim: Standards and advisory values change and differ by jurisdiction, so a memorised figure ages into a false statement
cons.example: quoting a limit from an older training manual after the regulator has revised it

failure_modes: presenting an aesthetic exceedance in health language
reporting a non-detect as absence
answering 'is my water safe' with anything other than the chemistry and a referral
acceptance_tests: every reported parameter is labelled with its standard class and compared against a value whose source and date are cited
no interpretation document contains a health-effect statement
non-detects are written with the method's reporting limit
revisit_triggers: a regulator revises a standard, adds a parameter or issues a new advisory value
a laboratory changes method reporting limits

nodes.definition: Hold the mechanism reference the entire offer rests on, class by class, expressed as what each one physically does and what it demands in return. Ion-exchange softening trades calcium and magnesium on a resin bed for sodium or potassium and regenerates with brine, so it genuinely removes hardness and returns an equivalent quantity of the exchanged ion to the water while producing a brine discharge whose disposal is governed locally. Salt-free scale conditioning of the template-assisted-crystallisation family converts hardness into microcrystals that resist adhering to hot surfaces, so scale is inhibited while hardness itself remains, a downstream hardness test still reads hard, and the slippery softened feel never arrives. Activated carbon adsorbs chlorine, tastes, odours and many organic compounds, with performance governed by contact time and bed life, while catalytic carbon is the sub-class reached for against chloramine and hydrogen sulfide. Sediment filtration is a micron-rated mechanical barrier and nothing more. Oxidation followed by filtration converts dissolved iron, manganese and sulfide into filterable solids and is sensitive to pH and to the oxidant chosen. Reverse osmosis drives water through a semi-permeable membrane that rejects a broad range of dissolved species and sends a reject stream to drain, normally serving one tap. Ultraviolet disinfection inactivates microorganisms in clear water and leaves no residual, so it requires sediment and iron pretreatment and a maintained lamp. Specialty media such as anion exchange for nitrate or iron-based adsorptive media for arsenic exist for named contaminants under named pH and speciation conditions.

included: per-class physical mechanism
what each class does not do
the preconditions and by-products each class imposes
the pretreatment relationships between classes
excluded: capacity sizing, flow rating and regeneration programming, which belong to the installation knowledge base
cartridge and media replacement scheduling, which belongs to the service-plan knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new media or treatment class entering the residential market, or repeated field underperformance of a class against its stated preconditions

pros.claim: Mechanism knowledge is what allows an honest claim to be made at all, because the claim is the mechanism
pros.example: explaining that a softener stops scale by removing the hardness ions rather than by 'purifying' the water

pros.claim: Knowing what each class does not do prevents the most expensive callbacks in the trade
pros.example: telling a scale-conditioning customer in advance that their hardness test will still read hard and their soap will not feel different

cons.claim: Mechanism explanations are longer than the marketing sentences customers arrive with, and some households simply want a verdict
cons.example: a customer who wants to know which box to buy losing patience during the difference between softening and conditioning

cons.claim: Class knowledge alone is not product knowledge, since two systems of the same class can differ sharply in media volume, valve quality and certified claims
cons.example: two ion-exchange softeners with identical mechanism narratives and materially different resin volumes and control valves

failure_modes: presenting scale conditioning as softening or letting the customer believe it is
specifying plain carbon where the district carries chloramine
proposing ultraviolet disinfection without the sediment and iron pretreatment its mechanism requires
acceptance_tests: each class in the reference states its mechanism, its preconditions, its by-products or discharge, and the parameters it does not address
the sales kit contains a written difference between softening and scale conditioning in customer language
revisit_triggers: a manufacturer introduces a class or media type the reference does not cover
field experience shows a class underperforming its stated preconditions in this territory's water

nodes.definition: Treat third-party certification as the only durable evidence behind a product claim, and learn to read it precisely rather than decoratively. Certification in this trade is organised by standard family - aesthetic-effects, health-effects, reverse-osmosis system, cation-exchange softener, ultraviolet, emerging-contaminant, and the material-safety and low-lead families that apply to anything plumbed into potable water - and is granted to a specific model, for specific claims, sometimes only when specific replacement elements are used. A certification mark on a carton is therefore never the answer; the searchable listing for that model and that claim is. The vetting routine opens the certifier's listing, records which contaminant-reduction claims are actually listed against which claims appear only in marketing, distinguishes a certified component inside an uncertified assembly from a certified system, files the listing reference with the quote, and re-checks it whenever a manufacturer revises a model or a listing lapses. Installed products also attract listing and material obligation classes under local plumbing rules; verifying and satisfying those belongs to the installation knowledge base, while this node owns the evidence that a claim is real.

included: standard families and what each covers
per-model, per-claim listing verification
system versus component certification
filing the listing reference with the quote and re-checking it
excluded: plumbing-code compliance and permitting for the installation
the wording of the claim itself, which the claim-boundary node governs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a model revision, a lapsed or narrowed listing, or a certifier changing a standard family

pros.claim: A verified listing turns a contested claim into a document, which is the only thing that survives a dispute
pros.example: answering a challenge to a contaminant-reduction claim by producing the certifier's listing for that exact model and claim

pros.claim: Vetting exposes the gap between marketing copy and listed claims before it reaches a customer
pros.example: finding that a brochure's contaminant list is far longer than the model's actual listed reduction claims and striking the difference from the quote

cons.claim: Rigorous vetting narrows the sellable catalogue and sometimes eliminates the cheapest option a price-shopping customer wants
cons.example: declining to quote an inexpensive unit whose contaminant claim is not listed for that model, and losing the job on headline price

cons.claim: Listings change without notice, so a verified claim can quietly go stale between quote and installation
cons.example: a model revision that carries forward the marketing name while the previous listing no longer applies

failure_modes: treating a certification mark on packaging as proof of a specific reduction claim
quoting a system claim supported only by a certified component inside it
letting a filed listing reference age past a model revision
acceptance_tests: every contaminant-reduction claim in a quote has the certifier's listing reference and retrieval date attached
no claim appears that is broader than the listed claims for that exact model
a periodic re-check confirms the listings behind currently quoted models are still current
revisit_triggers: a manufacturer revises a model, changes replacement elements or loses a listing
a certifier updates a standard family or its listing structure

nodes.definition: Map only confirmed problems onto the treatment classes that verifiably address them, and refuse to map anything else. The mapping runs from evidence - a dated hardness figure, a free-versus-total chlorine determination, an iron and manganese result read alongside pH, a laboratory nitrate, lead or arsenic value, a coliform result - to a mechanism family and its preconditions, and it carries an explicit anti-pattern list drawn from the trade's most common mis-sales: a softener sold to fix chlorine taste, whole-house reverse osmosis proposed as a hardness solution, activated carbon offered against nitrate, ultraviolet disinfection installed with no sediment or iron pretreatment behind visibly cloudy water, scale conditioning sold to a household that was promised the softened-water feel, and arsenic media selected without regard to speciation and pH. Its output is a ranked, evidence-linked recommendation set in which every proposed stage names the parameter it addresses and its supporting document, every precondition is stated, and every complaint that no proposed stage addresses is written down explicitly as unaddressed rather than quietly dropped.

included: evidence-to-class mapping with preconditions
the named anti-pattern list
ranking of stages and the unaddressed-complaint register
excluded: where in the house each stage goes
capacity, flow and regeneration sizing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a contradicting laboratory result, or post-install evidence that a mapped class failed to resolve its target parameter in this territory's water

pros.claim: Requiring a document behind every stage makes over-specification visibly indefensible inside the company
pros.example: a proposed iron filter that cannot name a result is struck from the recommendation at review

pros.claim: The unaddressed-complaint register prevents the most common post-install disappointment
pros.example: writing plainly that the whole-house system will not change the taste at the kitchen tap and that a drinking-water stage is the option that would

cons.claim: Strict mapping can leave a genuine but unmeasured complaint unaddressed and the customer unsatisfied
cons.example: an intermittent seasonal odour that no sample has caught, so nothing can be honestly proposed for it yet

cons.claim: Multi-parameter water forces sequencing and interaction judgements that a simple mapping table understates
cons.example: iron and hardness together, where pretreatment order and resin fouling change what the softener can be expected to survive

failure_modes: mapping from a symptom or a customer phrase rather than from a dated result
ignoring a precondition such as pH, turbidity or speciation that governs whether the class works
silently dropping a complaint nothing proposed will fix
acceptance_tests: every stage in the recommendation names its target parameter, the dated evidence for it, and the precondition it depends on
the anti-pattern list has been checked against the proposed set and the check is recorded
every complaint raised by the household appears as addressed or explicitly unaddressed
revisit_triggers: a laboratory result arrives that contradicts the evidence the mapping was built on
post-install feedback shows a mapped stage did not resolve the parameter it targeted

nodes.definition: Decide where in the dwelling each confirmed problem should be treated, which is a separate decision from what class treats it. Point-of-entry treatment earns its place when the problem damages the plumbing system or affects every outlet: scale reaching the water heater, valves and appliances, iron or manganese staining laundry and fixtures, chlorine noticeable in showers, or a microbiological risk on a well that must be handled before distribution. Point-of-use treatment is the honest answer when the concern is drinking and cooking water alone, which is where a certified reverse-osmosis or contaminant-specific drinking-water system belongs, and it is frequently the smaller, cheaper and correct recommendation that a margin-driven habit would skip past. Many households legitimately need both, in a defined order with a defined relationship between the stages. The scoping decision also absorbs the household's real constraints - a homeowner-association or condominium restriction, a rented dwelling, no drain within reach, an unheated garage, a crawl space - and records each as a constraint for the installation knowledge base to resolve rather than as a reason to quietly drop a confirmed finding.

included: the treat-at-the-house versus treat-at-the-tap decision rule
stage ordering when both are needed
constraint capture for the installation team
excluded: physical placement, drain routing, bypass configuration and permits
consumable scheduling for each stage

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: installation-stage discovery of a constraint that invalidates the scoping decision, or a change in household use

pros.claim: Scoping to the smallest sufficient footprint is the clearest signal of an evidence-led company and it wins referrals
pros.example: recommending only an under-sink drinking-water system where the sole confirmed issue is a drinking-water parameter, despite a whole-house sale being available

pros.claim: Explicitly recording constraints prevents an installation being sold that the property cannot accept
pros.example: flagging that the only viable location has no drain, so the drain question is answered before any date is offered

cons.claim: The smaller scope leaves other complaints untouched and can read to the customer as an incomplete solution
cons.example: a household delighted with their drinking water and still annoyed by shower scale that nothing was proposed for

cons.claim: Two-stage scoping raises total complexity and introduces interactions the customer must understand
cons.example: a whole-house system feeding a drinking-water system whose own replacement schedule differs from the house filter's

failure_modes: defaulting to whole-house scope because it is the larger sale
proposing point-of-use treatment for a problem that is damaging the plumbing system
carrying a constraint in a technician's memory instead of in the file
acceptance_tests: each confirmed problem in the recommendation is assigned a treatment location with a stated reason
every household constraint discovered is written into the file with the decision it affects
where both scopes are proposed, the stage order and the relationship between them is stated
revisit_triggers: a constraint discovered at installation contradicts the scoping decision
the household's use pattern changes, such as a new occupant, appliance or additional bathroom

nodes.definition: Assemble the recommendation into a small number of packaged options a homeowner can genuinely compare, each internally coherent rather than deliberately crippled. A workable architecture presents an entry option that solves the confirmed primary problem with a certified system and nothing else; a middle option that solves the primary problem and the secondary one the evidence also supports, typically whole-house treatment plus a drinking-water stage; and an upper option that adds capacity, media grade, monitoring, or warranty depth for households that value them. Every tier states which parameters it addresses, which it does not, what startup consumables are included, and what ongoing replacement it will require - handing the design of the service plan itself to the retention knowledge base rather than improvising one at the kitchen table. Tier differentiation must be a real difference in mechanism, capacity, certified claim or warranty; discount ladders, invented premium tiers built to be rejected, and options whose only difference is price are prohibited, because they convert an evidence-led recommendation back into the pressure sale the diagnostic process exists to replace.

included: tier composition and the rule that each tier is internally coherent
per-tier statement of addressed and unaddressed parameters
startup consumables and the pointer to ongoing replacement
prohibition of decoy tiers and discount-ladder differentiation
excluded: service-plan tier design, pricing and renewal, owned by the retention knowledge base
the cost build-up behind each tier's price

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a tier that is never chosen or always discounted, or a change in a product's certification or warranty that alters what a tier can claim

pros.claim: Comparable options move the conversation from yes-or-no pressure to a choice the household controls
pros.example: a customer choosing the entry system now and adding the drinking-water stage the following year, with both already scoped

pros.claim: Stating per-tier limitations in writing pre-empts the most common source of post-install disappointment
pros.example: the entry tier stating plainly that it addresses scale and does not change drinking-water taste

cons.claim: Tiering invites decoy design, and the temptation to build a top tier nobody should buy is constant
cons.example: an upper option padded with monitoring hardware that adds no capability the household's evidence justifies

cons.claim: Three options can overwhelm a household that wanted a recommendation, pushing the decision to no decision
cons.example: a customer deferring indefinitely because they cannot judge whether the middle option's extra capacity matters

failure_modes: differentiating tiers by discount rather than by mechanism, capacity, certified claim or warranty
hiding the consumable obligation in the tier that looks cheapest
presenting tiers before the evidence and mapping are complete
acceptance_tests: each tier names the parameters it addresses and does not address, its certified claims, and its startup and ongoing consumables
the difference between adjacent tiers is a stated difference in mechanism, capacity, certification or warranty rather than price alone
no tier exists that the company would not recommend to a household whose evidence pointed at it
revisit_triggers: a tier is chronically unsold or chronically discounted, indicating it was built as a decoy
a product's certification or warranty terms change under a tier

nodes.definition: Understand a quote as a build-up of real, documented inputs rather than a number lifted from a rate card. The cost stack for one job is equipment at the operator's current distributor tier plus freight and any drop-ship charge; installation labour measured as crew-hours for this specific configuration at a fully loaded rate that includes vehicle, insurance and non-billable time; fittings, valves and materials; the subcontracted-plumber or permit line wherever the local requirement class applies; startup consumables and the first media or cartridge charge; a warranty and callback reserve informed by the operator's own callback history rather than by hope; and the allocated acquisition cost of the marketing and free-testing activity that produced this lead. Margin moves whenever any of those move - distributor tier shifts with purchase volume, install hours fall with crew experience and rise sharply with retrofit difficulty, callbacks consume the reserve, consumer financing carries a dealer participation cost that must be treated as a cost and disclosed, and seasonal demand changes how much idle crew time each job carries. Every input is verified for the specific deal against the actual distributor quote, timesheet, permit receipt and finance schedule; nothing here is a remembered figure. The consumable annuity that follows the sale has its own economics and belongs to the retention knowledge base.

included: the per-job cost stack and its documentary sources
the levers that move margin
financing participation treated as a disclosed cost
the per-deal verification rule
excluded: service-plan and consumable annuity economics
any stated industry-standard price, margin or commission figure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a distributor, freight, labour, permit-fee or finance-participation change, or measured drift between assumed and actual install hours and callbacks

pros.claim: A documented build-up lets the operator discount, decline or walk away with knowledge instead of instinct
pros.example: recognising that a difficult crawl-space retrofit has consumed the job's margin in labour hours before agreeing to match a rival's price

pros.claim: Treating finance participation as a cost stops a 'free financing' offer from silently eating the job
pros.example: pricing a long deferred-interest plan with its dealer participation cost visible in the build-up rather than discovered at month end

cons.claim: Rigorous job costing is administratively heavy for a small operator and decays the moment timesheets stop being honest
cons.example: install hours recorded as the scheduled two rather than the actual five, which quietly corrupts every future quote

cons.claim: Margin pressure pushes toward larger systems, so the cost model must be paired with a rule that the evidence, not the margin, sets the scope
cons.example: an upsell that improves job margin while addressing no parameter the testing confirmed

failure_modes: quoting from a remembered price rather than the current distributor quote
omitting the permit or subcontracted-plumber line where the requirement class applies
carrying no callback reserve and funding warranty work out of the next job
acceptance_tests: every quoted job's cost stack cites the distributor quote, labour estimate, permit or subcontract line and finance schedule it was built from
no figure in the build-up is stated without a document behind it
the callback reserve is derived from the operator's own recorded callback history
revisit_triggers: a distributor changes tier, price or freight terms
actual install hours or callback rates drift from the assumptions in the build-up
a finance partner changes its dealer participation terms

nodes.definition: Produce a single written artifact from which the homeowner, the spouse who was not home, the installer and, if it ever comes to it, a consumer-protection officer would all reach the same understanding. The packet attaches the dated evidence - screening form, utility report extract, laboratory report with its chain of custody - and states for each proposed component the parameter it addresses and the certification listing that supports the claim; it itemises equipment, installation labour, any permit or subcontracted-plumber line, and startup consumables so the customer can see what they are buying rather than a single lump sum; it says in plain words what the system will not do, including every complaint left unaddressed and anything that needs a plumber, a well contractor or further testing; it sets out the ongoing replacement and service obligation the chosen classes create without designing the plan itself; and it carries the warranty terms, the financing disclosures where financing is offered, and the written cancellation-rights notice required by the home-solicitation obligation class in your jurisdiction, whose current form and timing must be verified locally.

included: attached dated evidence
per-component parameter and certification statement
itemised pricing and startup consumables
the will-not-do section
warranty, financing and cancellation-rights disclosures as obligation classes to verify locally
excluded: service-plan enrolment terms and pricing
installation scheduling and scope-of-work drawings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the local home-solicitation, financing or warranty disclosure requirement class, or a dispute exposing ambiguous packet language

pros.claim: A written packet outlives the visit and the representative, which is what makes an evidence-led sale durable
pros.example: a customer who cancels a competitor's contract after comparing two documents and finding only one names the parameters and their evidence

pros.claim: The will-not-do section converts the most expensive future complaint into a signed acknowledgement
pros.example: a signed line stating the whole-house system does not change drinking-water taste, produced when that complaint later arrives

cons.claim: A thorough packet is long, and length itself can stall a decision or invite line-by-line price attack
cons.example: an itemised labour line becoming the focus of negotiation while the certified system's value goes undiscussed

cons.claim: Disclosure obligations differ by jurisdiction and product, so one template silently becomes wrong when the company crosses a boundary
cons.example: a cancellation notice built for one jurisdiction accompanying a sale made in a neighbouring one with different requirements

failure_modes: quoting a lump sum with no itemisation or evidence attached
omitting the cancellation-rights notice required for an in-home sale
describing ongoing consumables vaguely so the recurring obligation surprises the customer later
acceptance_tests: every packet contains the dated evidence, per-component parameter and certification references, itemised pricing, the will-not-do section, warranty terms and the applicable cancellation-rights notice
no packet contains a health claim or a claim broader than the attached listing supports
the ongoing consumable obligation is stated in plain language even though the plan is designed elsewhere
revisit_triggers: a jurisdiction served changes its home-solicitation, financing or disclosure requirement class
a customer dispute reveals an ambiguity in the packet's language

nodes.definition: Choreograph the appointment so the pressure comes out of the room without the professionalism going with it. The protocol opens with disclosure - who the company is, that it sells and installs treatment equipment, what the testing costs or does not cost, and roughly how long the visit will take - and takes explicit permission to enter, to sample and to photograph.
